# Finding the Antiderivative of -x^5·sin(3x)

I'll use the **tabular method** (repeated integration by parts) to compute this.

## Setting Up the Tabular Method

**Derivatives** of x^5 (differentiate repeatedly):

| Step | Derivative |
|------|-----------|
| 0 | x^5 |
| 1 | 5x^4 |
| 2 | 20x^3 |
| 3 | 60x^2 |
| 4 | 120x |
| 5 | 120 |

**Integrals** of sin(3x) (integrate repeatedly):

| Step | Integral |
|------|----------|
| 0 | sin(3x) |
| 1 | -cos(3x)/3 |
| 2 | -sin(3x)/9 |
| 3 | cos(3x)/27 |
| 4 | sin(3x)/81 |
| 5 | -cos(3x)/243 |

## Applying the Tabular Formula

$$\int x^5 \sin(3x)\,dx = x^5\cdot\frac{-\cos(3x)}{3} - 5x^4\cdot\frac{-\sin(3x)}{9} + 20x^3\cdot\frac{\cos(3x)}{27} - 60x^2\cdot\frac{\sin(3x)}{81} + 120x\cdot\frac{-\cos(3x)}{243} - 120\cdot\frac{-\sin(3x)}{729}$$

Simplifying:

$$= \frac{-x^5\cos(3x)}{3} + \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} + \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} - \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} - \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} + \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243}$$

## Negating for -x^5·sin(3x)

$$\int -x^5\sin(3x)\,dx = \frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3} - \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} - \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} + \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} + \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} - \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243} + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result, all intermediate terms cancel and we recover **-x^5·sin(3x)** ✓
